description: Task execution process logging (Phase 1): capture ops command output line-by-line in the runner, store it on an independent server channel, and render it in the Web task expand area.

tasks.title: Server: TaskLog independent persistence and query API
tasks.description: Add a dedicated TaskLogEntries store (entity + EF Core migration) under Infrastructure/Data/Runner/, a TaskLogStore with append and cursor-paginated query, and two HTTP endpoints: a dual owner-kind POST upload route mirroring artifact uploads, and an issue-path GET query that resolves taskId (TaskRun.Id) to workId and returns { lines, nextCursor, truncated }. The store writes directly with no grain involvement. Register TaskLogStore in DI.
acceptanceCriteria: TaskLogEntryRow entity exists with columns Id (PK), OwnerKind, OwnerId, WorkId, Seq, Timestamp, Source, Text (no stream column); EF migration creates the TaskLogEntries table with an index on (OwnerKind, OwnerId, WorkId, Seq)

POST /api/workflow-runs/{ownerId}/work/{workId}/task-log and POST /api/agent-jobs/{ownerId}/work/{workId}/task-log persist entries directly to TaskLogStore via AppendAsync + SaveChangesAsync, never invoking WorkflowGrain or RunnerGrain.ReportWorkflowResultAsync

GET /api/projects/{projectId}/issues/{number}/workflow/tasks/{taskId}/logs resolves the workflow run (reuse ResolveWorkflowRunIdAsync) and taskId -> workId from run state, then returns { lines, nextCursor, truncated } with cursor pagination over seq
Pagination returns a non-null nextCursor when more lines remain and null on the final page; ordering by seq is stable and resumable
truncated is reported from the stored batch so the client can signal head lines were dropped at capture time
A task with no captured lines returns { lines: [], nextCursor: null } and never an error
report request body, WorkResult, and WorkflowRun aggregate structure remain unchanged (verified by existing server tests passing)

Server unit tests pass: store append/query returns entries in ascending seq order with seq/timestamp/source/text exposed; owner-kind routing keeps workflow vs agent-job entries from colliding; endpoint pagination and truncation flag behave per spec; upload independence from report verified
Existing server tests (npm test) do not regress
tasks.output: packages/server: TaskLogEntryRow.cs, TaskLogStore.cs, TaskLogRoutes (POST + GET), EF migration, DI registration; passing server unit tests
tasks.notes: Follow RunnerWorkStore.cs as the placement/store pattern and WorkflowArtifactUploadRoutes / IssueRoutes.Artifacts as the route pattern. taskId->workId resolution mechanism is an Open Question in design (D9): verify the workflow read model exposes WorkId lookup by TaskRun.Id without a grain call; if awkward, fall back to widening TaskStatusView with workId. Pick a concrete Text column type (nvarchar(max) vs capped) consistent with the head-drop capacity bound.

tasks.title: Runner: Ops command line-by-line capture engine
tasks.description: Upgrade runCommand (system/process.ts) with an optional onLine callback that emits merged stdout/stderr line-by-line with no-loss guarantees (trailing-newline flush + post-exit drain), preserving the existing aggregate CommandResult. Add ActionContext.log.write(source, text) as the single sink that masks known credential patterns before assigning a monotonic seq and buffering. Add a TaskLogCollector that buffers entries per work item, applies head-drop truncation on overflow, and exposes a terminal-batch flush. Add ServerConnection.uploadTaskLog for the independent upload channel.
acceptanceCriteria: runCommand with onLine emits every output line including a final line emitted without a trailing newline; a post-exit drain emits any buffered tail once after close so no line is lost
CommandResult (stdout/stderr/exitCode) is byte-identical whether or not onLine is supplied, so existing callers (git(), rebase/push/openspec/health-check) do not regress
log.write masks known credential patterns (git remote URLs with embedded credentials, runner-configured secrets) before assigning seq or buffering; no raw credential ever reaches the buffer
Each buffered entry carries a monotonic seq (within the work item), a timestamp from an injected clock (now: () => Date, no wall-clock), and a source label
TaskLogCollector drops oldest head lines on capacity overflow, keeps the most recent tail, sets a truncated flag, and does not reuse discarded seq values (retained seqs stay monotonic and contiguous)
Capacity limit is a single named tunable constant (e.g. MAX_TASK_LOG_LINES)
ServerConnection.uploadTaskLog posts the terminal batch to the owner-kind-appropriate task-log endpoint (workflow-runs vs agent-jobs, ownerKind computed as in artifact-side-effects.ts:107)

Runner unit tests pass: no-loss drain across close boundary, trailing-newline final line, masking-before-buffer, monotonic seq across multiple write calls, head-drop truncation with seq not reused, aggregate contract unchanged, timestamps from injected clock (vi.useFakeTimers + vi.setSystemTime)
Existing runner tests (npm test -w packages/runner) do not regress
tasks.output: packages/runner: runCommand.onLine in system/process.ts, TaskLogger + masker, TaskLogCollector, ActionContext.log in core/types.ts, ServerConnection.uploadTaskLog in server/connection.ts; passing runner unit tests
tasks.notes: Follow design D2 (single sink), D4 (onLine no-loss), D5 (mask at entry), D6 (head-drop truncation), D11 (injectable clock). The masker is intentionally minimal for Phase 1 (known patterns only; encoding-variant defense is future work). TaskLogger/TaskLogCollector must accept an injected now() threaded from the host like the existing n convention in workspace-registry.ts / worktree-enforcement.ts.

tasks.title: Runner: Wire ops executor phases to emit through the capture sink
tasks.description: Wire each executor phase to emit ops command output through ActionContext.log.write with a phase-appropriate source tag: prepareWorkspace -> workspace-prep, checkBranchStability -> branch-check, action body -> action:<name>, enforceCleanWorktree -> cleanup. Forward git() output line-by-line to the sink while preserving git()'s aggregate return contract. Create a per-work TaskLogCollector in the executor lifecycle and flush it once as a terminal batch in executeAndReport (best-effort: a failed upload is logged and swallowed, never blocking or failing the report).
acceptanceCriteria: Workspace preparation (git clone/checkout) output is tagged source workspace-prep and is captured rather than discarded
Branch-stability check output is tagged branch-check and clean-worktree enforcement output is tagged cleanup, both distinguishable from action body output
Action body ops commands (rebase, push, openspec, health-check) forward their stdout/stderr line-by-line to the sink tagged with an action source (e.g. action:rebase)
git() still returns its complete aggregate output unchanged so existing combinedOutput consumers do not regress
A per-work TaskLogCollector is created at the start of the work lifecycle and flushed once on task completion (success or failure) via ServerConnection.uploadTaskLog
The flush is best-effort: if the upload fails, the error is logged and swallowed and the report (which carries the verdict) still succeeds

Runner tests pass: phase source tagging verified for each phase, git() non-regression, best-effort flush (report succeeds when upload throws), a deliberately failing ops command's output reaches the collector buffer
Existing runner tests (npm test -w packages/runner) do not regress
tasks.output: packages/runner: executor phase wiring in runtime/executor.ts, flush in runtime/host.ts (executeAndReport), git() forwarding in actions/git.ts, workspace/branch-stability/worktree helpers updated; passing runner tests
tasks.notes: Follow design D6: flush happens in RunnerHost.executeAndReport around the existing report call, best-effort. The collector is created per work item alongside the existing report/artifact lifecycle. Ensure no ops output reaches the buffer by bypassing the sink (every emit path goes through log.write).

tasks.title: Web: Task execution log viewer panel
tasks.description: Add a TanStack Query hook that fetches task logs via the issue-path GET endpoint (keyed by issueNumber + taskId), and a log panel rendered inside TaskItem's expanded region (TaskProgressPanel.tsx) that displays captured lines line-by-line with source label and timestamp in a scrollable region. The panel is additive: existing status/message/output/failure-kind rendering remains unchanged. Surface a truncation indicator when the response reports truncated: true.
acceptanceCriteria: Expanding a task with captured logs renders each line with its source label, timestamp, and text in a scrollable region
A deliberately failing ops task (e.g. rebase conflict) exposes its real command output (conflicting commit, file, git error) by scrolling the panel
Each line's source label lets the user distinguish phases (e.g. workspace-prep vs action:rebase vs cleanup)
When truncated is true, the panel renders a truncation indicator and shows the retained tail lines
A task with no captured logs renders a graceful empty state (no error)
The log panel is additive: existing task status icon, title, message, structured output JSON, and failure-kind guidance render exactly as before
The query degrades gracefully to 'no log' if the endpoint is absent or returns empty
Web typecheck passes (npm run typecheck -w packages/web) and web tests pass (npm run test:run -w packages/web)
tasks.output: packages/web: TanStack Query hook for GET /api/projects/{projectId}/issues/{number}/workflow/tasks/{taskId}/logs, log panel component in TaskProgressPanel.tsx expanded region; passing web tests
tasks.notes: Follow design D10: the panel fetches via the issue-path query keyed by issueNumber + taskId. Render source label + timestamp alongside text per line. The query key should be [issueNumber, taskId] so it refetches when a different task is expanded. Existing rendering must remain unchanged (log is a fourth class of evidence, not a replacement).
